translations.text: As long as that people were willing to keep their fathers' covenant with him, God was their shepherd, the Guardian of the heavenly kingdom, the holy Lord, the Ruler of glory.

The Creator of all things gave that host courage and might, so that with the protection of their army they often took the lives of many peoples who were not loyal to them. This went on until pride came over them at the wine-feast, with devilish deeds and drunken thoughts.
Then the Lord of the kingdom grew fierce of mind, hostile to the people to whom he had given possessions.
He showed the war-path to the high city to foreign warriors, into the homeland where Jerusalem stood, skilfully fortified and honoured with walls.
Then, I have heard, the race of old enemies easily [?] the wine-city of men. Those warriors did not believe; they robbed Solomon's temple, the glory of the halls, of red gold, of treasure and silver.
They plundered the treasures under the stone cliffs, all such as the noblemen were to possess, until they had broken down every one of the strongholds that stood as protection for the people.

They loaded up as booty the treasure of the hoard-guardians, wealth and ornaments, whatever was found there. Then they journeyed back with the possessions, and they also led the race of Israel on a long journey, on the eastern ways to Babylon: a countless number of men, heroes under the hand of heathen rulers.
"Now you do not know my dream, you who bring me wisdom before the company."
Then the multitude in that meeting place could not, through prophecy, think out or devise anything at all, since they were prevented from telling the king his dream,
the mysteries of fate, until the prophet Daniel came to judgement. He was chosen by the Lord, wise and righteous, to go into that hall.
God gave him a gift from heaven through the utterance of the Holy Spirit, so that an angel of God told him everything his liege lord had dreamed.

Then, when day dawned, Daniel went to interpret the dream for his lord. He wisely told him the destiny of peoples, so that the strong-minded king at once understood the beginning and the end of what had been shown to him.
Then Daniel had great glory and renown in Babylon among the scholars, after he told the king the dream. Because of his sins, the guardian of Babylon had earlier been unable to take it into his heart.

Yet Daniel could not bring it about that he would believe in the Creator's might. Instead, he began to make an idol on the plain that the bold-minded called Dura, which was in the nation of that name, mighty Babylon.

The guardian of that city, the ruler of the realm, set up an image for men against the Creator's will, an idol of gold, because he was not wise but cruel and without counsel. Right [?] then the men listened, when the sound of the trumpet's voice came over the citizens.
The foreign nation, like their lord before them, committed folly and did wrong. (An evil reward came to them for it afterwards.)
When it had been heated as fiercely as he could with the dangerous flame of fire, he gathered the people there. The guardian of Babylon, grim and arrogant, ordered God's messengers to be bound.
The fire was kindled immeasurably great. Then the furnace was heated, the iron glowing all through. Many servants threw wood into it, as they had been ordered;

then the flame turned away from the holy ones onto the hateful men, the heathens. The youths were glad of heart. The servants burned outside around the furnace; the fire [?] turned to the harm of the malicious.
It was the God of glory who saved them from that hostility.
Then the holy Azarias spoke from his inmost thoughts through the hot flame. Eager for deeds, he endured [?], praised the Lord, a man without sin, and spoke these words: "Creator of all things, lo!
Your judgments are true every day, and mighty and victorious, just as you yourself are.

We are scattered across the wide earth, dispersed in crowds, without favour. Our life is despised and notorious in many lands, among many peoples, who have driven us into the power and possession of the worst of earthly kings,
into the captivity of the sword-fierce, and now we endure slavery to heathens. For this let there be thanks, King of glory of the hosts, that you appointed this punishment for us.

Do not abandon us, eternal Lord, for the sake of the mercies that men ascribe to you, and for the sake of the covenants that you, firm in glory, saviour from afflictions, Creator of spirits, made with Abraham and with Isaac and with Jacob.
You promised them by spoken word that in days of old you would increase their offspring, that after them it would be born in generations, and that the multitude would be great,

to be raised in station [?], like the stars of heaven that encircle the broad sky, or the sand of the sea-shores of the ocean-ways, which settles in the sea across the salt wave, so that its countless number would always grow through a multitude of years.

He thrust away the flame of the hot fire, holy and heaven-bright. Through his great might he swept away the gleam of the blaze and turned it aside, so that their bodies were not harmed at all. Instead, in anger, he struck the fire upon the enemies for their crimes.
There the three bold-minded men praised the Lord in their thoughts. The children of Israel called on all the creation of the earth to bless the eternal Lord, ruler of nations.
And the powers of the hearts of the holy, the souls and spirits of each of the righteous, praise you, Lord of life, who give reward to all the humble, eternal Lord!
May Hananiah and Azariah and Mishael glorify you, Creator, with the thoughts of their hearts!

Consider carefully who gave that gift to the young kinsmen! They praise God, the one eternal, and speak to him earnestly by every name of all things [?]. They thank him for his majesty with bold words, and say that he alone is almighty God, wise King of glory, of the world and of the heavens.

Their beauty was not marred, nor was there any damage to their clothing, nor was their hair singed by fire. Instead, in the Lord's protection, the wise-minded men stepped gladly out of the grim terror, in the Spirit's favour.
By that miracle he had honoured those who had earned it.

The youths praised the Lord before the heathen people. They taught him with true sayings and told him of many true signs, until he himself believed that the one who had rescued them from the darkness was the ruler of powers.
Their glory was in Babylon after they had endured the burning. Their fame was made known among the nobility [?] after they had obeyed the Lord.
Then, I have heard, after he perceived the wonder, the guardian of Babylon asked with true words how the three youths had come through the burning fire of the hot furnace, the sudden terror of fire.
Therefore he [?] reveals, through many a wonder, to the holy spirits who have chosen his favour.
Then a dream was revealed to Nebuchadnezzar in his sleep; it came close to him.

Then he commanded his people, the leaders of the nation, to gather together. The stern-minded king asked them all what the dream meant. This was not because he thought they knew it; he was testing how they would answer.
Then Daniel, God's messenger, was summoned to the judgment. A holy spirit from heaven had been given to him, and it strengthened his mind.
In him the Lord, the Guardian, knew a deep heart, broad thought, the skill of wisdom and wise speech. Often he revealed many a wonder, the powers of the Creator, before men.
Then the proud-hearted, heathen leader of the army began to tell of the terror of his dream, all the terror that had been shown to him.

He asked him to explain what the mystery meant, to lift up holy words and find in his mind how to say in true words what the tree that he had seen shining meant, and to foretell for him the course of what was fated.

and then he will live joyless among the wild beasts and dwell in the wilderness, and his root will be left in the earth, staying still in its place for a set time, as the voice said, until after seven seasons it receives seed again.

He will cut you off from the kingship and send you friendless into exile. Then he will turn your heart, so that you will not remember the joys of human company, nor know any understanding except the ways of wild beasts. Instead, you will live a long time and dwell throughout the forest, leaping like the harts.
My lord, think on firm counsel.

[?] what the war-leader had made for his troop through great wonder. Then he became arrogant above all men, overbearing in his heart, because of the special gift that God had given him: the kingdom of men, the world to rule over in the life of men.

Then the prince of the people no longer put off the words of the prophets. Instead, wherever he had the power to speak, he proclaimed far and wide the might of the Lord. He told his people of his journey, the far wandering he had gone through among the wild beasts, until a wise mind from the Lord God came into his spirit, when he looked up to the heavens.
So he eagerly preached the powers of the Lord to mankind, after Daniel had for a long while taught judgments to the city-dwellers in Babylon.
Then his third generation rose up in that nation.
He knew the nobles who were supposed to rule the kingdom to be in wrongdoing.

A sign came to him where he gazed, terrible before the nobles inside the hall, because he had spoken lying words before the people. There, to their terror, the angel of the Lord let his hand come into the high hall, and on the wall it wrote mysterious words in crimson letters for the city-dwellers.
Then they searched hard in the thoughts of their hearts for what the hand of the Holy Spirit had written.

Great power from God was in his spirit. I have heard that the guardians of the city eagerly tried to buy him with gifts, so that he would read and explain the letters to them and say what the mystery meant.
From these you began to drink to devils, these vessels that the Israelites once kept at God's ark as their law required, until boasting deceived them, a wine-drunk mind, as shall happen to you.
